title: 1951 AHSME Problem 11
statement: The limit of the sum of an infinite number of terms in a geometric progression is \(\dfrac{a}{1-r},\) where \(a\) denotes the first term and \(-1\lt r\lt1\) denotes the common ratio. The limit of the sum of their squares is:

solutions.text:
The squared terms form a geometric series with first term \(a^2\) and ratio \(r^2.\) Since \(|r|\lt1,\) its sum is \[ \frac{a^2}{1-r^2}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Squaring every term also squares the common ratio
